Run a database repository's post-build step

Source: R/process.R
build_post_process.Rd

A database repository may define post_build <- function(database) { ...; database } in R/post_build.R, for processing applied to the whole database once its datasets are combined, such as adding a column or moving a context into the traits table. Every pipeline build_setup_pipeline() writes calls this after build_add_version() and before the database is saved.

build_post_process(database, file = "R/post_build.R")

Arguments

database

Database object, as returned by build_add_version()

file

Path to the file defining post_build(). If the file does not exist, or file is character(0) (as the targets pipeline passes when there is no file), the database is returned unchanged and nothing is recorded.

Value

The database post_build() returned, with build_info$post_build added; or database unchanged if there is no file

Details

post_build() runs on every rebuild of the combined database, including a targets or remake rebuild after one dataset changes, so it should be quick. Outputs derived from the finished database that are wanted only when publishing it, such as a flattened copy or parquet files, belong in post_export() in R/post_export.R instead, which build_post_export() runs when asked and no build runs.

What post_build() returns replaces the database; there is no second, "processed" copy. It must therefore return the database, with every component it was given, and anything else is an error. Side effects, such as writing files, are allowed.

The file is sourced into a fresh environment whose parent is the search path rather than the global environment. post_build() sees attached packages (library(traits.build) attaches traits.build and its Depends), including any the file attaches with library() outside post_build(), and whatever the file itself defines, but not objects a pipeline happens to leave in the global environment, which differ between build.R and a targets worker. A package attached inside post_build() is not seen in a fresh session such as a targets worker: attach it at the top of the file, or call it as pkg::fun(). Other files in R/ are not sourced; source one from R/post_build.R if post_build() needs it. Only R/post_build.R itself is tracked, though: the targets and remake pipelines do not rebuild the database when a file it sources changes, and the md5 recorded below does not cover that file. Code that should trigger a rebuild belongs in R/post_build.R.

When the step runs, database$build_info$post_build records the file and the md5 checksum of its contents, so the code that last changed the database can be identified even when it was not committed. Line endings are normalised to \n before the checksum is taken, so a checkout with Windows line endings records the same checksum as one on macOS or Linux; for a file with \n endings it is the checksum tools::md5sum() gives the file.

See also

build_setup_pipeline(), build_add_version(), build_post_export()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In R/post_build.R
post_build <- function(database) {
  database$traits <- dplyr::mutate(database$traits, curve_id = NA_character_)
  database
}

# In the pipeline, after `build_add_version()`
database <- build_post_process(database)
database$build_info$post_build
} # }
